title: Chapter 24 — Smart Home and Connected Appliances
intro: What smart features actually do, honest use-case selling, privacy, and integration.

sections.title: What Smart Actually Means
sections.content:
Smart appliances connect to Wi-Fi and offer features like remote monitoring, diagnostics, notifications, and app control. Some integrate with voice assistants. Some offer recipe guidance or automatic cycle selection.

The key question during discovery: does the customer actually want smart features? Some love them. Some do not care. Some are actively resistant. Sell smart features to the customers who value them. Do not push them on customers who do not.

sections.title: The Honest Conversation
sections.content:
Smart features add cost. They also add complexity — app setup, Wi-Fi requirements, firmware updates, privacy considerations. Be honest about what smart features do well and where they add friction.

The customer who buys a smart refrigerator and never connects it to Wi-Fi did not get value from the smart features. The customer who checks their fridge camera from the grocery store every week did. Know the difference.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating smart appliance knowledge, ask:

Does the salesperson gauge customer interest in smart features during discovery — or assume everyone wants them?
Can they demonstrate smart features on the showroom floor?
Are they honest about the trade-offs — cost, complexity, privacy?
Do they sell smart features as benefits that fit the customer's lifestyle — not just technology for technology's sake?
